items.title: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen
items.description: As we have learnt from two individuals affected, Swiss police authorities use an enormous amount of violence during forced deportations. From the perspective of lawyers and Swiss human rights organisations, the authorities are thereby committing massive violations of Swiss and international law. Furthermore, in at least two cases, they have put the lives of those affected at serious risk. Augenauf shares this assessment and has informed the relevant authorities (including the commander of the Zurich cantonal police and the National Commission for the Prevention of Torture, NKVF). Bot
items.titleIt: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen

items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: Sudan: Sudan's Civil Society Groups Reject El Burhan's Mooted Dialogue As 'Political Cover'
items.description: [Dabanga] Khartoum -- Sudanese civil society coalitions and actors, the Darfur Women Platform, Sudan Civic Convergence Tracks, Sudan Peace Call, Tadamon, and Union's Front, have issued a categorical rejection of a proposed Sudanese-Sudanese dialogue sponsored by Gel Abdelfattah El Burhan and the country's military leadership, warning that a political process organised under the authority of one of the parties to the war cannot deliver either peace or legitimacy.
items.titleIt: Sudan: Sudan's Civil Society Groups Reject El Burhan's Mooted Dialogue As 'Political Cover'

items.title: Ethiopia: Amid Escalating Federal-Tigray Tensions, Debretsion Says Alliance Has Become 'Irreversible'
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Amid escalating tensions and renewed clashes between Ethiopia's federal forces and Tigrayan forces, Tigray Government President Debretsion Gebremichael (PhD) has said an alliance formed with other political and opposition forces has become institutionalized and "irreversible," with its own leadership, plans and signed agreement, according to Weyin Media.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Amid Escalating Federal-Tigray Tensions, Debretsion Says Alliance Has Become 'Irreversible'

items.title: Uganda: Government Dismisses Claims Tooro Queen Mother Is Under House Arrest
items.description: [Nile Post] Government has dismissed reports circulating on social media that Tooro Queen Mother Best Kemigisha has been placed under house arrest amid growing tensions and divisions within the kingdom following the death of King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV.
items.titleIt: Uganda: Government Dismisses Claims Tooro Queen Mother Is Under House Arrest

items.title: IPI: Africa Media Freedom Monitoring: April to June 2026
items.description: The International Press Institute (IPI) recorded nearly 100 cases of threats and attacks on journalists (82 male and 18 female) across 22 countries in sub-Saharan Africa between April and June 2026. Physical and verbal attacks, as well as arrests and detention, were the most frequent types of incidents. An Ethiopian journalist in exile was found dead in Kenya under suspicious circumstances.   Police and state security forces (55%) continued to be the primary perpetrators of attacks and threats against journalists, a trend that continues from the previous quarter.
